features.name: Lecture 2 (harness-creator): Tools subsystem permissions block
features.description: Lecture 2's five-subsystem model (Instructions/Tools/Environment/State/Feedback) has two subsystems the Lecture 1 scorer never measured: Tools and Environment. Added a .claude/settings.json permissions.deny rule enforcing one of AGENTS.md's four 'Boundaries' (never write AGENTS.override.md). First draft used a single-* glob and an ask-rule on install.sh/install-agents-md.sh; codex-kiro (a genuinely different model, not another Claude instance) reviewed it and found both broken -- the glob does not cross path segments, and the ask-rule is trivially bypassed by any invocation form other than the exact literal matched (compounded by this host's permissions.defaultMode=auto). Both findings independently confirmed (a local glob fixture test, not accepted on say-so) before fixing: widened to **, and removed the ask-rule entirely in favor of documenting that boundary as advisory-only in AGENTS.md, rather than pretending an unenforceable rule enforces it. Full writeup: docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/.
features.evidence: jq -e '.permissions' .claude/settings.json -> valid, deny-only. `bash scripts/run-tests.sh --fast` -> 53 passed, 0 failed, both before and after the codex-kiro-driven fix. Environment subsystem (.python-version, dependency-manifest/osv-scanner question) explicitly left open -- see docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/summary.md.

features.name: Resolve Lecture 2's two open findings: real dependency manifest + stale mypy.ini comment
features.description: Built an isolated .venv (from the already-pinned 3.14.7 interpreter, not the shared ambient pyenv environment) with only this repo's actual dev deps (mypy, ruff, pytest, lxml, anthropic, google-generativeai). Generated requirements-dev.txt via `.venv/bin/pip freeze` -- osv-scanner now genuinely scans it (confirmed via verbose output: 'found 51 packages') and reports clean, no CVE fixes needed (the earlier CVE list came from the polluted ambient environment's older pins, not this repo's real deps). Rewired only the two real gates that need third-party packages (types-guard.sh, run-tests.sh) to prefer .venv/bin/* with a bare-interpreter fallback; confirmed via a full call-site audit that every other python3 invocation in the repo either ships to other people's machines (must stay on ambient PATH) or only needs stdlib (no change needed). Fixed test_types_guard.sh's literal-string assertion for the new invocation form. Updated mypy.ini's comment and AGENTS.md's osv-scanner section to describe the new real state. Also resolved codex-kiro's third Lecture-2 finding (python-version-vs-mypy.ini tension): the two settings were never actually in conflict -- mypy still infers from whichever interpreter runs it, pinned or not -- the original comment's portability rationale was just less load-bearing now that .venv standardizes contributors on one interpreter. docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/ updated to record both findings as resolved rather than parked.
features.evidence: `osv-scanner scan source --recursive . --verbosity error` -> No issues found (verbose form confirms requirements-dev.txt was actually scanned, 51 packages, not the 'no package sources found' bypass). `bash .claude/hooks/tests/test_types_guard.sh` -> 9/9 passed. `bash scripts/run-tests.sh --fast` -> 53 passed, 0 failed. `.venv/bin/mypy` and bare `mypy` (ambient PATH, still resolves 3.14.7 via .python-version) give identical clean results, confirming the fallback doesn't silently change behavior. `bash .claude/hooks/secret-scan.sh` run manually end-to-end (the one path with zero prior test coverage) -> exit 0, both gitleaks and osv-scanner OK.

features.name: Close the version-drift/silent-fallback gap in feat-007's .venv preference logic (multi-model review)
features.description: Reviewed feat-007's fallback pattern with codex-kiro (failed once with a hard stream error, succeeded on retry) and agy (a third, genuinely different model family -- brought in specifically because codex-kiro had just failed once). codex-kiro found a real gap: '[[ -x "$MYPY" ]] || MYPY="mypy"' only proves executability, not that the venv is the right Python version -- a stale/rebuilt .venv would silently be used with zero warning. Fixed in types-guard.sh and run-tests.sh: both now compare .venv's actual python3 --version against .python-version and fail loud (exit 2 for the Stop-hook gate, exit 1 for the CLI) on any mismatch or broken binary, instead of silently falling back to ambient tooling. Confirmed by actually simulating drift (echo 9.9.9 > .python-version) and watching it block, not just reading the code. agy required --dangerously-skip-permissions to run at all in headless mode; its review then produced two confident but FALSE claims (Python 3.14.7 'does not exist' -- installed and used all session; httpx2/httpcore2 are 'potential typosquats' -- both real PyPI packages, a legit anthropic transitive dep per pip show/pipdeptree) which were checked and refuted, not accepted. One claim converged across both models and checked out against PyPI directly: google-generativeai is genuinely deprecated (legacy, support ended 2025-11-30, successor google-genai) -- flagged as a real, confirmed, NOT-yet-actioned finding since migrating it touches shipped code (polish_engine.py), a different-shaped change than this session's scope.
features.evidence: Simulated version drift (`echo 9.9.9 > .python-version`) -> `bash .claude/hooks/types-guard.sh` exits 2 with rebuild instructions, `bash scripts/run-tests.sh --fast` exits 1 with the same, both correctly refusing to silently fall back; restored the pin, reran clean. `bash scripts/run-tests.sh --fast` -> 53 passed, 0 failed after the fix. `pip show httpx2`/`pipdeptree --reverse -p httpx2` confirmed agy's typosquat claim false. WebFetch on pypi.org/project/google-generativeai/ confirmed the deprecation claim true. google-generativeai -> google-genai migration explicitly NOT done -- open finding for a future session, recorded in docs/harness-creator/lecture-02/summary.md and progress-detail.md Part 8.
